_comment: Real secrets (DB password, JWT signing key) are NOT in this file — it's committed to a public repo. They live in appsettings.Production.json (gitignored, exists only on the machine that publishes) which ASP.NET Core layers on top of this file automatically when ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production. See back-end/README.md.

ConnectionStrings.DefaultConnection: Server=(set in appsettings.Production.json, not committed);Database=db62877;User Id=db62877;Password=(set in appsettings.Production.json);Encrypt=False;MultipleActiveResultSets=True;TrustServerCertificate=True

Jwt.Secret: (set in appsettings.Production.json, not committed — must be 32+ chars)

GoogleAuth._comment: Web OAuth Client ID from Google Cloud Console (Credentials > OAuth client ID > Web application). Not secret — safe to commit; it's the public identifier the front-end also uses (NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID). Deliberately does NOT include the client secret: this flow verifies the id_token straight off Google's JWKS (AuthService.ValidateOidcIdTokenAsync), no server-side authorization-code exchange, so no secret is needed here at all.

AppleAuth._comment: Services ID from Apple Developer > Certificates, IDs & Profiles > Identifiers, with Sign in with Apple enabled (Domains: project-web-frontend-two.vercel.app, Return URL: https://project-web-frontend-two.vercel.app). Also not secret — same identifier the front-end uses (NEXT_PUBLIC_APPLE_CLIENT_ID). No private key (.p8) needed here: the front-end's popup flow hands us Apple's id_token directly, verified against Apple's public keys — no server-side client_secret exchange.
